text.p: Singapore's Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) has charged three former directors of trading-based Amcol Holdings with breach of duties as directors, a CAD spokesman said on Wednesday.
Chng Heng Tiu, Jhonny Kesuma and Kang Thian Leng face four charges each of having breached their duties as Amcol directors in 1994.
The three were charged in a Singapore Subordinate Court on Wednesday and released on bail.

According to the charge sheets, Chng, Kesuma and Kang "failed to act honestly" in the discharge of their duties as Amcol directors over the remittance of US$7 million to a company called PT Amcol Graha Electronic Industries.
The money was "purportedly for the purpose of funding Amcol Graha in a venture to provide satellite television and radio broadcast services in Indonesia", the charge sheet said.
The CAD spokesman said the next hearing would be on February 12.
Under Singapore law, the maximum penalty for breach of director's duties is a fine of up to S$5,000 and one year's imprisonment.
There is also the possibility of being disqualified from being a director for up to five years.
